description: SPECTRAL PEAK STREAMS, mode 4 (time-invariant summary): parses the whole analysis file, finds the most-visited semitone regions (the prominent pitch-streams), then writes each stream's AVERAGE pitch and relative amplitude to a text DATA file - one 'frq<TAB>amp' line per stream, amps normalised to the loudest = 1.0 (verified on a 220 Hz harmonic tone: 6 streams, '223.48 0.105 / 893.31 0.228 / ... / 2225.33 1.000'). With -f the same data is written as a 2-line filter varibank file (times 0 and 1000, verified), with -m as MIDI values - so the output feeds filter varibank/userbank directly. Modes 1-3 share the argv (1 = per-window time-varying peak list, 2/3 = time-varying pitch-stream assignment); mode 4 pinned as the always-small, always-non-empty summary. Deterministic. The duration_model 'static' is a schema placeholder - data outputs skip the audio pre-flight.
musical_use: Distil a sound's resonant identity into a handful of numbers: the average pitch-streams ARE the sound's stable partials/formant positions, ready to seed a filter bank (write the -f varibank form and hand it to filter varibank; or the plain form to filter userbank) so any other material can be filtered through THIS sound's resonances. winsiz is the semitone granularity of the peak search; peak sets how much louder than the window's median a channel must be to count (raise it to keep only true peaks); floor discards everything below a fraction of the file's maximum; lo/hi confine the search band. -h with a tune value discards peaks that are harmonics of stronger peaks (keep only fundamentals of parallel streams); -q quantises the reported pitches to quarter-tones and -m converts to MIDI for pitch-data workflows. For evolving sounds where streams move, use sibling modes 1-3 via execute() - mode 4 deliberately averages that motion away.

winsiz.description: Semitone width of the window used to search for peaks (CDP-enforced 1-96, refusals at 0/97 verbatim). Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 ... brkpnt_files not permitted.').

peak.description: A channel must be this many times louder than the median of all channels in the window to count as a peak (CDP-enforced 1-1000, refusal verbatim).

floor.description: Peaks must exceed floor * (max channel amp found anywhere in the file) to be retained (CDP-enforced 0.0001-1, refusal verbatim '(0.000100 to 1.000000)').

lo.description: Minimum frequency to accept as a peak (CDP-enforced analysis-channel-width to nyquist - refusal verbatim '(43.066406 to 22050.000000)' at pvoc anal 1 defaults; input-dependent).

hi.description: Maximum frequency to accept as a peak (same input-dependent bounds as lo).

tune.description: If non-zero, any peak that is a harmonic of another peak (within 'tune' semitones) is discarded; 0 retains all peaks (banner range 0-6). Verified accepted.

lose_amps.description: Discard the amplitude information (frequency column only; with -f, all varibank amps become 1.0).

quantise.description: Quantise reported frequencies to the tempered scale, in quarter-tones.

varibank.description: Write in filter varibank format (verified: two identical 'time frq amp frq amp ...' rows at times 0 and 1000) - directly consumable by filter varibank. Cancels -z.

examples.description: Harvest a sound's average resonance table.
examples.expected_use: Output .txt: one 'frq amp' line per prominent stream, loudest = 1.0. Feed to filter userbank.

examples.description: Straight to a varibank filter definition.
examples.expected_use: Two-row varibank file; hand it to filter varibank to filter other material through this sound's resonances.

known_issues: DATA OUTPUT (.txt): 'frq<TAB>amp' per stream (or MIDI with -m; 2-row varibank with -f) - filter-bank food, not audio. Duration pre-flight skipped; duration_row null in the findings (no audio duration).
Reserved audio extensions refused for the output ('ERROR: Cannot open a textfile (pko.wav) with a reserved extension.' verbatim) - the engine names data outputs .txt, which CDP accepts.
lo/hi bounds are input-dependent (analysis channel width to nyquist).
Mode 4 assumes a relatively constant spectrum (banner) - it averages stream motion away; time-varying stream data lives in sibling modes 1-3 (mode 1's per-window peak counts vary; 2/3 stream them).
Deterministic (byte-identical text run to run). Bool switches are execute()-side until the engine accepts bools.
